svg.aria-label: How the block-height colour adapts to the rolling median fee. Two identical colour bars run from blue through green, a plateau at the median in the user's configured base colour, then yellow, orange and red. The first bar is labelled for a quiet network with a 30-day median of 2 sat per vByte, the second for a busy network with a median of 20. Because the scale is anchored to the median, the same 3 sat per vByte reads red and expensive on the quiet network but blue and cheap on the busy one. The bars show the softened tones actually rendered on a light theme rather than the raw scale. Below, three panels show what 3 sat per vByte means against each median, that the base colour is configured per theme and appears at the top of the digits on a dark theme and the bottom on a light one, and sample block-height digits carrying the base colour at one end and the fee at the other.
svg.text: Block height colour — relative to the rolling median fee
The colour does not track the fee. It tracks the fee against what fees have been doing lately — the median
of the last 30 days. Both bars below are the same scale. Only the numbers underneath them change.
